corrections.source_says: The entire ten-person experiment is not established as an RCT. Use other, described as a partly randomized supervised remote experiment: four students with creative-writing experience were explicitly randomized, two to ChatGPT and two to no AI, but assignment of the remaining students is not stated. The explicitly randomized subgroup qualifies the paper for two-screener review; retain unclear for the full-sample random-assignment eligibility criterion and null for the total number randomized.
corrections.quote: the four students who answered that they had some experience were randomly distributed between the 2 groups—two in Group 1 (which collaborates with AI) and two in Group 2 (which does not collaborate with AI).
corrections.locator: PDF pp. 2-3, Section 3.1 Sample; p. 3, Sections 3.2-3.3; p. 5, Table 3; p. 6, Table 5

corrections.form_value: Ten Polytechnic students were split into two groups of five. Group 1 used ChatGPT (GPT-3) and Group 2 worked without AI on two remote tasks over WebEx: Guilford's Alternative Uses Test (two 4-minute phases, six objects) and a 20-minute 'What would happen if...' rewrite of the myth of Perseus and Andromeda. AUT answers were scored for fluency, flexibility, and originality by the test manual, stories by a 3-level rubric on the same three traits, and the group totals were compared with Mann-Whitney U tests.
corrections.source_says: Replace the claim that group totals were compared with Mann-Whitney U tests with participant-level total scores were compared between groups. Tables 3 and 5 each report five valid observations per group; Tables 4 and 6 test Total_score. The sums displayed in Graphs 1 and 2 are separate descriptive summaries of the component scores.
corrections.locator: PDF p. 5, Tables 3-4; p. 6, Tables 5-6 (table images inspected directly); p. 4, Graph 1; p. 5, Graph 2

confirmed: Source version, title, and authors match the journal article: Vasiliki Kollia and Dimosthenis Manias, EAI Endorsed Transactions on Creative Technologies, Volume 11, 2025, DOI 10.4108/eetct.10417; received 13 November 2024, accepted 04 November 2025, published 11 November 2025 (PDF p. 1). The PDF has 10 pages; all markdown and PDF pages, including appendices and references, were read.

Appendix A contains Group 1 storytelling prompts and Appendix B contains the evaluation rubric; both are inside the PDF, with no separate supplement mentioned (PDF pp. 8-9; references to appendices on pp. 3-4).

Ten Polytechnic students participated, and both outcome tables show five valid people and zero missing observations in each group; n_analyzed=10 and five per arm are correct, with no exclusions reported (PDF p. 2, Section 3.1; p. 5, Table 3; p. 6, Table 5).

Random assignment is explicitly stated for four experienced writers, two per arm; the full-sample randomized count is not reported. The existing assignment narrative accurately identifies this limitation (PDF pp. 2-3, Section 3.1).

Group 1 used ChatGPT, described by the article as OpenAI's GPT-3 language model, while Group 2 worked without ChatGPT; this is human AI assistance, not an AI-versus-human output benchmark (PDF p. 3, Section 3.3).

Both tasks used the same participants in remote WebEx sessions: AUT had two phases of four minutes each and six objects, with up to six alternative uses per object; storytelling allowed 20 minutes to rewrite the myth of Perseus and Andromeda (PDF p. 3, Sections 3.2-3.3).
AUT reported descriptive statistics all match: Group_1 mean 63,80, SD 17,079, median 71,00, N 5; Group_2 mean 34,40, SD 10,090, median 36,00, N 5 (PDF p. 5, Table 3).

AUT reported tests all match: Mann-Whitney U ,500; Wilcoxon W 15,500; Z -2,514; Asymp. Sig. (2-tailed) ,012; Exact Sig. [2*(1-tailed Sig.)] ,008, with the table footnote stating Not corrected for ties (PDF p. 5, Table 4).
Storytelling reported descriptive statistics all match: Group_1 mean 4,40, SD 2,608, median 3,00, N 5; Group_2 mean 5,20, SD 1,789, median 5,00, N 5 (PDF p. 6, Table 5).

Storytelling reported tests all match: Mann-Whitney U 8,000; Wilcoxon W 23,000; Z -,976; Asymp. Sig. (2-tailed) ,329; Exact Sig. [2*(1-tailed Sig.)] ,421, with the table footnote stating Not corrected for ties (PDF p. 6, Table 6).

The AUT originality reported string is numerically correct: Group 1 versus Group 2 sums are 47 versus 38 for originality, 140 versus 68 for fluency, and 132 versus 66 for flexibility (PDF p. 4, Graph 1). These are score sums, not participant counts.
The one-line finding accurately reports AUT means 63.80 versus 34.40 with asymptotic p=.012, and storytelling means 4.40 versus 5.20 with asymptotic p=.329 (PDF p. 5, Tables 3-4; p. 6, Tables 5-6).

Core eligibility remains no because only ten people were analyzed; the output-scoring criterion is met, and context_class=none is appropriate for this small, partly randomized assistance experiment (PDF pp. 3-6, methods, scoring, and Tables 3-6; codebook Sections 3-4).

This is an empirical experiment with a background literature review, not a pooled-effect synthesis. The review mentions 10 studies but supplies no pooled estimate, interval, or standardizer (PDF p. 2, Section 2; pp. 3-7, experiment methods and results).
summary: Reported statistics match the PDF, but design qualification, analysis-unit wording, omitted outcomes, and statistics flags need correction. Four students were explicitly randomized, warranting two-screener review; ten were analyzed overall, below the eligibility threshold.
